quests.instruction: A bakery wants to bring fresh bread to lots of small shops across town every morning. Which vehicle suits the job?
quests.hint: It needs a big space for trays and boxes, not for passengers.
quests.explanation: Delivery trucks carry goods from where they are made to where they are sold. A closed back keeps the bread clean and dry.
quests.funFact: Many bakeries start baking before sunrise so the bread can reach shops by morning.

quests.instruction: A courier must deliver an envelope across a busy city centre where cars are stuck in jams. Which vehicle can weave through?
quests.hint: It is narrow enough to pass between rows of traffic and needs no fuel.
quests.explanation: Bicycles are narrow, so couriers can slip through traffic and use cycle lanes. For short city trips they are often as quick as cars.
quests.funFact: Bicycle couriers have delivered messages in busy cities for well over a century.

quests.instruction: A delivery company drops parcels at front doors all day along quiet neighbourhood streets. Which vehicle do they usually use?
quests.hint: It has a roomy back for parcels but is small enough to park on a street.
quests.explanation: A van holds lots of parcels yet is small enough to stop outside homes. Bigger trucks would be hard to park in narrow streets.
quests.funFact: Delivery drivers plan their routes so they stop at addresses in the most sensible order.

quests.instruction: A family is moving to a new house 500 kilometres away. Which vehicle can carry their sofa, beds, and boxes?
quests.hint: It needs a very large, strong back space and a powerful engine.
quests.explanation: A large truck can carry furniture and many boxes in a single trip. A car or scooter would need many journeys.
quests.funFact: Moving companies wrap furniture in blankets and straps so it does not slide around.

quests.instruction: Fresh flowers picked in Kenya must reach a shop in Europe within a day or two. Which is the quickest way?
quests.hint: Flowers wilt quickly, so speed matters most.
quests.explanation: Flowers and other fresh foods spoil quickly. Planes cross continents in hours, which is why they are used for goods that cannot wait.
quests.funFact: Many cut flowers travel in the cargo hold of passenger planes alongside suitcases.

quests.instruction: A heavy machine must reach a mountain hut where no road goes. Which vehicle can lift it there?
quests.hint: It can carry loads hanging below it on a long cable.
quests.explanation: Some helicopters carry heavy loads on a long hook. They can place materials where no truck can drive.
quests.funFact: Helicopters have helped to lift materials for mountain huts, bridges, and power lines.

quests.instruction: Many people live in a town 40 kilometres from a big city and travel to work every day. Which is a good regular choice?
quests.hint: It runs on a regular timetable along its own track, away from road jams.
quests.explanation: Commuter trains carry lots of workers on regular timetables. They avoid road traffic and make long daily trips easier.
quests.funFact: Some commuter trains in big cities carry more than a thousand people.

quests.instruction: It is late at night, the buses have stopped, and a family needs to get home from a party. What can take them door to door?
quests.hint: You can call or hail one at almost any hour, and it goes straight to your home.
quests.explanation: Taxis run at any time and go exactly where you ask. They are handy when buses and trains are no longer running.
quests.funFact: Many taxis show a light on the roof to say they are free to hire.

quests.instruction: Hundreds of holidaymakers want to sleep, eat, and swim on board while visiting several ports. Which vessel is made for this?
quests.hint: Think of a floating hotel with lots of decks.
quests.explanation: A cruise ship is like a floating holiday resort. It carries passengers from port to port while they relax on board.
quests.funFact: Some cruise ships have room for several thousand passengers.

quests.instruction: Thick smoke is pouring from the window of a house. Which emergency vehicle should be sent?
quests.hint: Water and hoses will be needed first.
quests.explanation: Fire engines carry water, hoses, and trained firefighters. Their job is to put out fires and rescue people from danger.
quests.funFact: In many countries, one phone number such as 112, 911, or 999 connects callers to the emergency services.

quests.instruction: A person has fainted on the pavement and will not wake up. Which emergency vehicle should be sent?
quests.hint: Someone with medical training needs to reach them quickly.
quests.explanation: An ambulance brings paramedics, who give treatment and can take the person to hospital. Calling quickly can help a lot.
quests.funFact: Ambulances carry equipment such as oxygen and defibrillators.

quests.instruction: A child is lost in a crowded market and cannot find their family. Which helpers can be called to search and keep them safe?
quests.hint: These helpers keep the community safe and can search the area.
quests.explanation: Police officers help find missing people and look after those in trouble. Staying calm and telling a trusted adult is the first step.
quests.funFact: Many police forces advise lost children to look for an adult in uniform or a shop worker.

quests.instruction: After a big concert, thousands of people must leave the city centre at the same time. Which can carry the biggest crowds along a fixed route?
quests.hint: Think of the one that runs many carriages along its own line.
quests.explanation: Metro trains carry huge numbers of people at once. Taxis or motorbikes would need thousands of separate journeys.
quests.funFact: Some big stations run extra trains after large events to carry crowds home.

quests.instruction: A visitor wants to see an old city from an open-top ride while a guide talks about the sights, together with other tourists. Which vehicle is that?
quests.hint: It has many seats and goes slowly past the main attractions.
quests.explanation: Sightseeing buses carry many tourists along a route past the main sights. Some have open tops for better views.
quests.funFact: Many cities have hop-on, hop-off buses, where you can get off at a sight and catch the next bus later.

quests.instruction: A worker finishes a train journey and needs to cover the last kilometre to the office. They want to fold the vehicle up and carry it on board. What fits?
quests.hint: It is light, has small wheels, and can be folded.
quests.explanation: Folding scooters are light and small, so people can carry them onto trains and buses and ride the last part of a journey.
quests.funFact: Many train companies allow folding scooters and bicycles to be carried on board.

quests.instruction: A farmer needs to carry sacks of grain across bumpy tracks from the field to the barn, with an open back for easy loading. Which vehicle suits best?
quests.hint: It is sturdy, with a car-like front and an open space behind.
quests.explanation: A pickup truck is strong enough for rough farm tracks, and its open bed makes loading sacks and tools easy.
quests.funFact: Some pickups can also tow trailers carrying animals or machines.

quests.instruction: In many villages, farmers use this strong animal to pull ploughs and carts. Which is it?
quests.hint: It has horns and works slowly and steadily.
quests.explanation: Oxen are strong, calm animals that can pull heavy loads. In places where tractors are rare or costly, they still help with farm work.
quests.funFact: A pair of oxen joined by a wooden yoke can pull a plough through hard soil.

quests.instruction: Some farmers hire small aircraft to spray crops over huge fields from above. Which aircraft is used for this?
quests.hint: It is small enough to fly low and close to the crops.
quests.explanation: Agricultural aircraft fly low and cover large fields quickly. Pilots spray water, plant food, or crop-protection liquids.
quests.funFact: Aircraft that spray crops are sometimes called crop dusters.

quests.instruction: Which piece of equipment protects your head if you fall off a bicycle or scooter?
quests.hint: It is hard on the outside and fastens with a strap under your chin.
quests.explanation: A helmet cushions your head in a fall. It must fit well and be fastened correctly to work.
quests.funFact: Helmets are tested by dropping them onto hard surfaces.

quests.instruction: Which bright jacket with shiny stripes helps drivers see people walking or working near the road?
quests.hint: It glows when headlights shine on it.
quests.explanation: High-visibility clothing stands out in daylight and reflects headlights at night. Road workers, cyclists, and walkers wear it.
quests.funFact: The shiny stripes bounce light straight back toward the car that shone it.

quests.instruction: Which small item helps a walker or rider see the path and be seen on a dark road?
quests.hint: Press a button and it makes a beam.
quests.explanation: A torch lights up the path ahead and helps others notice you. Riders should also have lights on their bikes at night.
quests.funFact: Many bicycle lights can flash, which makes riders even easier to notice.

quests.instruction: A fast train takes two hours for a trip that takes five hours by car. What does the train save?
quests.hint: Look at the clock, not the fuel gauge.
quests.explanation: Choosing a quicker way to travel saves time. People pick fast trains for long trips because they arrive sooner.
quests.funFact: Some high-speed train journeys between cities can be quicker than driving or flying once airport waiting is added.

quests.instruction: Eight friends share one minibus to a festival instead of hiring eight taxis. What do they save?
quests.hint: Splitting the cost leaves more in everyone's pocket.
quests.explanation: Sharing a vehicle splits the cost between everyone. Public transport and shared rides are often cheaper than travelling alone.
quests.funFact: Sharing rides, called carpooling, also means fewer cars on the road.

quests.instruction: A bicycle trip does not need something that a petrol car needs for every kilometre. What is it?
quests.hint: You fill a tank with it at a pump.
quests.explanation: Petrol cars burn fuel to move. Bicycles use your muscles, so there is nothing to buy at the pump.
quests.funFact: A bicycle is one of the most energy-efficient ways to travel.

quests.instruction: A container ship is loaded with thousands of big metal boxes. What do these boxes mostly carry?
quests.hint: Think of the things sold in shops, like clothes, toys, and machines.
quests.explanation: Container ships carry goods packed in standard boxes, so they can be moved easily by ship, train, and truck.
quests.funFact: Shipping containers come in standard sizes, so cranes, trucks, and trains around the world can handle them.

quests.instruction: A tanker lorry delivers fuel to petrol stations. Which picture shows what it carries?
quests.hint: It is a liquid stored in a drum or tank.
quests.explanation: Tankers carry liquids like fuel, milk, or water in a sealed tank. The tank keeps the liquid safe and stops it spilling.
quests.funFact: Fuel tankers have separate sections inside, so the liquid does not slosh around too much.

quests.instruction: A truck is backing up to a field after the harvest to be loaded. Which picture shows the crop it collects?
quests.hint: It grows in fields and is used to make bread, rice, and cereal.
quests.explanation: Farm trucks carry harvested crops to mills, stores, and markets. Different crops need different trucks to keep them fresh or dry.
quests.funFact: Grain trucks are often covered to keep rain from spoiling the crop.

quests.instruction: Which fun ride runs on tracks and is built to thrill people, not to take them anywhere?
quests.hint: It twists, loops, and climbs high, then drops quickly.
quests.explanation: A roller coaster runs on rails like a train, but its purpose is excitement rather than travel.
quests.funFact: Many roller coasters use gravity. A lift pulls the cars to the top, then they roll down.

quests.instruction: At a summer lake, a family wants a fast, fun ride that can pull a water-skier. Which vessel suits that?
quests.hint: It has a strong motor but is small enough to turn quickly.
quests.explanation: A speedboat has a powerful motor and can pull skiers or tubes behind it. Large ships are built for cargo or passengers.
quests.funFact: Water-skiers wear life jackets, and a spotter watches them from the boat.

quests.instruction: Which rider is pedalling along a bumpy forest trail on a strong, chunky-tyred bike?
quests.hint: Thick tyres grip the dirt, and the rider's own legs do all the work.
quests.explanation: A mountain bike has wide tyres and strong parts for bumpy ground. Riders pedal along trails for fun and exercise.
quests.funFact: Mountain biking has been an Olympic sport since 1996.
